bullets.title: SNOW: Blockbuster Q1 +34% product rev growth; PT raises flood in from $260–$325
bullets.body: Snowflake delivered 34% Y/Y product revenue growth ($1.33B, beat by ~5%), driven by Cortex Code (7,100+ accounts) and Snowflake Intelligence. Q2 guided +30% Y/Y vs. ~26% consensus; FY27 raised to $5.84B (+31%). Signed $6B multi-year AWS deal, best-ever net new product revenue of $108M. PT upgrades include: UBS $325, Wolfe $310, MS $300, Mizuho $295, Piper/OPCO $295, KeyBanc $285, Goldman $278, Citi upgraded to Buy $260. Stock +35-38% pre-market.

bullets.title: MRVL: FY28 revenue raised to $16.5B (+45% YoY); interconnect +70%; PT upgrades across the Street
bullets.body: Marvell beat/raise with FY27 revenue guidance $11.5B (+40% YoY) and FY28 $16.5B (+45% YoY); data center to grow 50% in FY27 and 55% in FY28. Interconnect growth guidance raised to +70% Y/Y (from +50%). Custom XPU to double in FY28 targeting $10B by FY29. PT raises: Roth $275, OPCO $250, Wolfe $250, UBS $230, Citi $225, KeyBanc $260, MS (EW) $195. LITE/COHR backlogs extend to CY28 corroborating optical demand thesis.

bullets.title: CRM: In-line Q1 with Agentforce ARR >$1B; Street skeptical on 2H acceleration; PT mixed
bullets.body: Salesforce beat Q1 (rev +12% YoY CC, EPS $3.88 vs $3.13), Agentforce ARR $1.2B (+205% Y/Y), but cRPO/billings light and FCF guided +4-5%. Q2 revenue guide $11.27-11.35B seen as light; management dropped explicit 'organic re-acceleration in 2H' bullet despite verbal confidence. Bulls (KeyBanc OW $290, Wolfe OW $220, Mizuho OW $250, Piper OW $215) see Agentforce inflection; bears (UBS Neutral $185, Citi Neutral $187-188, DA Davidson Neutral) cite 6-8% organic growth trough and core deterioration in Service/Tableau.

bullets.title: META: KeyBanc upgrades to OW $760; subscription launch seen as $8B+ revenue opportunity
bullets.body: KeyBanc upgrades META to Overweight at $760 PT (22x 2027 P/E), modeling $18-20B annual subscription revenue across consumer Plus ($4B), AI tiers ($7B), Creator/Business ($5B+), and Essential ($2B). Seven subscription SKUs launched globally at $2.99-$49.99/month. Mizuho also upgraded to Outperform; JPM notes $8.6B annualized revenue at 5% DAP penetration with ~90% incremental margins (+9% boost to 2026E OI). CEO also signaling cloud computing ('MetAWS') optionality if data center overcapacity materializes. APP +10% as META backs away from non-IDFA mobile ad market.

bullets.title: DELL: Wins $9.7B Pentagon contract for Microsoft software license consolidation
bullets.body: Dell Technologies awarded a $9.7B US military contract to consolidate Microsoft software licenses across the DoD, expected to save the Pentagon $422M annually. Stock +4.4% pre-market. Citi buyside expectations for April quarter: $3.30+ EPS on $40B+ revenue vs. consensus $2.96 on $35.74B; FY27 Citi est $13.09 on $142.5B above company guidance.

bullets.title: MU: DA Davidson raises PT to $1,500; Mizuho raises to $1,150; HBM/AI memory supercycle
bullets.body: DA Davidson raised MU PT from $1,000 to $1,500 citing HBM codesign into data center architecture and unjustified CPU/memory valuation gap (MU at 9x vs AMD/INTC at 40x). Mizuho raised PT to $1,150 on 90% CAGR HBM TAM through 2028E and HBM4e pricing up 70-100% Y/Y in 2027. DRAM/NAND ASPs expected at +308%/+256% in 2026E; retail flows at +3.4z this week; MU crossed $1T market cap.

bullets.title: NVDA: Jensen teases unannounced product; GPU-to-GPU hybrid bonding tests underway; Rubin CPX reportedly cancelled
bullets.body: Jensen Huang stated at Computex that NVIDIA has a surprise new product not yet disclosed. Sell-side notes NVIDIA testing GPU-to-GPU hybrid bonding (N1/N1X most likely candidate). Separately, Citi Korea notes Rubin CPX inference GPU effectively cancelled with no GDDR7 memory or substrate orders placed; Groq LPU placed at forefront of Vera Rubin platform following $20B deal. Computex/GTC Taipei (Jun 1-4) remain key catalyst events.

bullets.title: SHOP: UBS deep-dive sees POS scaling from 12% to ~20% of GMV; adds 300-500bps to GMV CAGR
bullets.body: UBS detailed analysis shows Shopify's in-store POS business currently ~12% of GMV with potential to approach 20% by 2035, contributing 300-500bps to 10-year GMV CAGR of 15-21%. Shopify holds only ~1% of US in-store retail TAM vs. ~14% in eCommerce, with recent Estée Lauder wins signaling mid-market penetration. UBS maintains Neutral rating.

bullets.title: ARM/INTC/AMD: Wolfe models agentic CPU TAM +30% through CY28; AMD biggest EPS winner
bullets.body: Wolfe analysis: Agentic and orchestration CPUs drive ~30% CPU TAM growth through CY28. AMD server CPU revenue expected at $44B by CY28 (vs $17B CY26), adding $7 incremental EPS to lift earnings power to $25-30. ARM modeled at $1.25 incremental EPS from datacenter royalties + silicon for ~$4.50 CY28 earnings power, with 50% ARM share scenario in agentic CPUs by CY28. INTC faces share loss risk to Google Axion but has spare fab capacity optionality.

bullets.title: FSLR: Upgraded to Buy at GLJ Research with $315 PT (15% upside)
bullets.body: GLJ Research upgraded First Solar to Buy from Hold, raising PT to $315 from ~$208, implying 15% upside from $273.67. The upgrade comes ahead of expected co-located data center generation serving 22-32 GW by 2030.

bullets.title: TTD: Rothschild initiates at Sell with $11 PT (51% downside); OMC Neutral $89
bullets.body: Rothschild & Co Redburn initiated The Trade Desk at Sell with an $11 price target, representing 51% downside vs. FactSet average of $25.82. Omnicom Group initiated at Neutral with $89 PT (19% upside).

bullets.title: TSLA: Robotaxi incident rate improved 3x to ~150K miles/incident; FSD at 26.7M miles/day
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley notes TSLA robotaxi incident rate improved dramatically from ~50K miles between incidents (late 2025) to ~150K miles in Q1 2026. FSD miles driven reached 26.7M miles/day (up from 18.5M in April); 33 active unsupervised robotaxis as of May 27.

bullets.title: FOXA/TKO/ROKU/CMCSA: FIFA World Cup 2026 seen as major media tailwind
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley models $300-400M+ in World Cup advertising revenue for FOXA; TKO's OnLocation hospitality could see +$75M EBITDA tailwind with 2x sales vs. prior World Cups. ROKU benefits from Fox One FAST channel launch at $19.99/month. CMCSA has Telemundo Spanish-language rights. MS Economics forecasts +10-15bps consumption boost in June/July.

bullets.title: AVGO: Earnings on June 3; JPM flags as key catalyst with semis at +75% YTD
bullets.body: AVGO reports June 3 per JPM macro calendar. JPM notes SOX semiconductor index up 75% YTD, biggest gains since dotcom, and flags AVGO earnings as the next major semis catalyst. MU +19.3% and SOXX +6.1% already extreme YTD; bullish but prudent to consider hedges on further appreciation.

bullets.title: DELL earnings tonight: buyside expects $3.30+ EPS on $40B+ vs. Street $2.96/$35.74B
bullets.body: Citi notes buyside bar for Dell April quarter is materially above consensus: $3.30+ EPS on $40B+ revenue vs. consensus $2.96 on $35.74B. July quarter buyside expects $3.50+ on $41B+ vs. Street $3.05/$35.3B. Pentagon contract win already known but AI server demand the key narrative.

bullets.title: CIEN: Raymond James reiterates Outperform ahead of July 7 investor day
bullets.body: Raymond James analyst Simon Leopold reiterates Outperform on Ciena, constructive on F2Q26 results due July 7. Near-term upside constrained by supply availability despite strong hyperscale demand; key investor focus on supply chain execution, gross margin progression, and evidence of sustained hyperscale demand into FY27-28.

bullets.title: IONQ: $470M backlog and superior revenue scale vs. peers; quantum complex in focus
bullets.body: IONQ generates $64.7M revenue/quarter with $470M contract backlog vs. INFQ's $9.5M revenue at similar forward P/S. Quantum stocks surged 15-65% after $2B DoC deployment announcement. IONQ pre-market -2.9% as broader quantum complex consolidates; retail flows elevated across the complex.

bullets.title: INTC: Investing billions in EMIB advanced packaging as cost-competitive TSMC alternative
bullets.body: Per Korean media reports, Intel is investing several billion dollars in EMIB packaging technology, positioned as better cost/productivity vs. TSMC's 2.5D silicon interposer approach. Intel also planning large-scale silicon capacitor adoption in AI chips starting next year. Foundry revival strategy accelerating via advanced packaging infrastructure.

bullets.title: UBER: Raises Delivery Hero stake to ~37%; acquisition intent probable
bullets.body: Uber raised its stake in Delivery Hero from ~25% to ~36.8-37% via ~€40/share Aspex acquisition, controlling 24.99% voting rights and potentially blocking rival bids. JPM notes acquisition intent is probable. Stock context: UBER also raised Amazon stake in LEO satellite reseller agreement in Japan separately.

bullets.title: SNOW/CRM/software peers: Broad software rally with MDB +9.5%, NET +3.3%, NOW +4.8%
bullets.body: SNOW's blowout quarter is catalyzing a broad software sector re-rating in pre-market: MDB +9.5%, NOW +4.8%, NET +3.3%, TEAM +2.4%, ADBE +2.0%, HUBS +1.9%. UBS analyst Keirstead notes 'software stock-picking matters again' and maintains preference for Data/Infrastructure layer (SNOW, DDOG-like platforms) over application software. CRM +0.8% on mixed reception.
